claim: The All-changes caption reads "Flat activity feed — what changed, when, by whom. Persisted per user, so the view you left is the view you return to."
truth: Nothing persists it. The feed is a projection of an in-memory undo stack that is emptied and re-seeded on every project load, so on every reload the list is EMPTY — the user returns to "No undo history", not to the view they left. Nothing about it is per-user either; it is per-tab.
evidence: HistoryManager.ts:34 `private undoStack: HistoryEntry[] = []` — the file imports no storage module at all (imports at :20-27 are EVENTS/THRESHOLDS, shared types, deepClone, OTTypes, Composer, HistoryFormatter, historyTypes, JsonPatch; no localStorage/indexedDB/STORAGE_KEYS reference anywhere in engine/HistoryManager.ts or engine/HistoryFormatter.ts). HistoryManager.ts:156-160, on EVENTS.PROJECT_LOADED: `this.undoStack = []; this.redoStack = []; this.patchesSinceCheckpoint = 0; this.currentStateCache = null; this.recordCheckpoint("loaded")`. HistoryFormatter.ts:21 `for (let i = undoStack.length - 1; i >= 1; i--)` skips index 0, so a stack holding only the load checkpoint yields zero rows. useHistoryState.ts:45-50 reads `composer.history.getHistoryStack()`; ActivityView.tsx:695 then renders "No undo history" with the hint "Use Ctrl+Z to undo changes".
edit: 172:3 text node — replace the whole caption with: "Session-only activity feed, derived from the undo stack: what changed and when, in this tab. The project load resets the stack, so this list is empty after every reload — it is not persisted, and not per user." Do NOT touch 163:2 (founder-settled 2026-09-02).

claim: Neither 172:3 nor any board in section 16 states a ceiling on the changes list.
truth: The undo stack is hard-capped at 100 entries and the oldest are shifted off silently at the moment they become unreachable. The event written to announce that is declared and never emitted.
evidence: HistoryManager.ts:613-629 `trimHistory(){ while (this.undoStack.length > this.config.maxHistory) { const removed = this.undoStack.shift(); … } }`, called from record() at :230; HistoryManager.ts:82 `maxHistory: THRESHOLDS.HISTORY_MAX_SIZE`; config.ts:108 `HISTORY_MAX_SIZE: 100`. Searched by CONSTANT, not by call site: `HISTORY_CAPACITY_WARNING` has exactly ONE reference in packages/editor/src — its own declaration at events.ts:133 — so it is neither emitted nor listened for.
edit: Append one sentence to 172:3: "The stack holds the last 100 steps; older ones are dropped with nothing said, so a named version is the only thing that survives a long session." COMPANION NODE, same pass if section 23 is in scope: caption 814:7065 (S3.9 · undo-redo-toast) says "Stack depth: 100 actions per session, pruned on save" — the 100 is right, "pruned on save" is wrong (trimming runs on every record; saving never touches the stack).

claim: The prune notice reads "Past 50. Named versions and the approved one were kept." and its caption 172:8 repeats it: "named and approved versions never prune."
truth: There is no approval protection, and nothing in the version model knows what approval is. The prune keeps named versions only. The same board's own footer already states the real rule — "named ones never prune" — so the board contradicts itself in two places 600px apart.
evidence: The copy ships verbatim at VersionHistoryPanel.tsx:391. Both prunes protect `isAutoCheckpoint` and nothing else: VersionHistoryStorage.ts:236-238 `versions.filter((v) => v.isAutoCheckpoint).slice(-excess)`; server side site-version.service.ts:79-82 `all.filter((r) => r.isAuto).slice(-excess)`. NamedVersion (shared/types/versions.ts:19-42) has no approval field and neither does the Prisma row (schema.prisma:1105-1120 SiteVersion: id, siteId, versionId, name, isAuto, payload, createdBy, createdAt). Approval is fetched separately from the review status and carries no version id — SavesChrome.tsx:73-83 `fetchReviewStatus()`, and its own docblock at :68-71 says `reviews.status` carries state, reviewer and time, not a version number.
edit: 163:269 body text → "Past 50. Named versions were kept." And caption 172:8 → "Cap 50. Auto-saves prune oldest-first; named versions never prune. Approval is not tracked per version, so it protects nothing — say so, or people assume it does."

claim: The confirm reads "Restore v3?" / "Your current work is saved as v4 first — nothing is lost.", and caption 172:6 restates it as the sentence that makes the button safe to press.
truth: Three separate problems. (1) The safety version IS taken, so half the promise is real. (2) "nothing is lost" is false: the snapshot is exportProject() and nothing more, so restoring rolls back pages, styles, settings, metadata and CMS bindings while CMS records, media assets and saved components — three separate IndexedDB databases — stay where they are; a restored page can come back bound to a collection field or an asset that no longer exists. (3) The confirm cannot say "v4": the safety version is created AFTER the confirm and is named `Before restoring "<name>"`, and the shipping panel deliberately omits the name for that reason.
evidence: Safety save: VersionTimelineManager.ts:289-299 creates `Before restoring "${version.name}"` and returns false if it throws. Snapshot scope: VersionTimelineManager.ts:160 `captureSnapshotAsync()` → Composer.ts:611-635 exportProject returns {version, pages, styles, assets: [] (:616), metadata, settings, cmsBindings} — no collections, no components, no media. Restore writes only that: VersionTimelineManager.ts:307 `this.composer.importProject(deepClone(version.snapshot))`, and Composer.ts:542-606 importProject touches elements, styles, cmsBindings, settings and metadata and consults no sibling store. The siblings live in their own databases: ComponentStorage.ts:15 `aquibra-components`, cms/CollectionStorage.ts:13 `aquibra-cms`, media/IndexedDBAdapter.ts:44 (DB_CONFIG.name). The "v4" name: VersionHistoryPanel.tsx:352-357 comment plus the shipped string at :364 — "Your current work is saved first — nothing is lost."
edit: 163:167 line 2 → "Your current work is saved as a version first. Pages, styles and brand settings are replaced; your content records, media library and saved components are not." Drop the invented "v4" (the name is not known at confirm time). Caption 172:6 → same two facts. See W-H-17 for the SEPARATE time-travel confirm — this row is only about the versions.restoreVersion path.

claim: "Ctrl+Shift+T turns the list into a scrubber; the canvas previews the hovered entry behind a 44h bar. Nothing is written until Restore."
truth: The canvas never previews anything. The preview mechanism is an fed from a version's visualSnapshot, and no version ever has one — the capture looks up an element id that exists nowhere in the codebase, and auto-checkpoints hardcode null anyway. The preview layer is therefore permanently at opacity 0, and scrubbing changes only the label in the drawer while the canvas keeps showing the present. The band and the "Nothing is written until Restore" sentence are real; the preview is not.
evidence: VersionTimelineManager.ts:991-999 captureVisualSnapshot → :993 `document.getElementById("editor-canvas")`, :994 `if (!canvas) return null`. A repo-wide grep for the string "editor-canvas" in packages/editor/src returns FOUR readers (VersionTimelineManager.ts:993, ActivityView.tsx:46, TimeTravelScrubber.tsx:157 and :162) and ZERO writers — no id="editor-canvas" is rendered anywhere, and the canvas mounts engine HTML in a div, not a <canvas>, so toDataURL was never the right mechanism. Auto-checkpoints set it null unconditionally: VersionTimelineManager.ts:237 `visualSnapshot: null`. Downstream: TimeTravelScrubber.tsx:54 `if (!v.visualSnapshot) continue`, :112 `setPreviewSrc(nearest?.visualSnapshot ?? null)`, :233-239 `else { layer.style.opacity = "0" }`. Same root cause disables the Saves compare diptych: CompareView.tsx:90 `hasVisual = Boolean(version.visualSnapshot || currentVisualSnapshot)` and :117 `disabled={!hasVisual}`.
edit: 172:5 → "Ctrl+Shift+T opens a scrubber drawer over the canvas. It moves through the undo stack by time and shows the entry's label — the canvas itself does NOT change while scrubbing; only Restore writes. There is no frame preview: no version carries a visual snapshot." Keep the band on 163:113 as drawn.

claim: 163:113 draws only the 280px panel band that appears while time-travel is on. The scrubber itself — the thing Ctrl+Shift+T opens — is drawn nowhere in the section's 34 boards.
truth: The scrubber is a modal bottom drawer over the canvas with its own controls, its own empty state, and its own keyboard contract, none of which has art.
evidence: HistoryTab.tsx:378-386 mounts <TimeTravelScrubber> at panel level whenever showScrubber. TimeTravelScrubber.tsx:304-377 renders: a backdrop `.tt-overlay` that activates on drag (:307-310); a `role="dialog" aria-modal="true" aria-label="Time travel"` drawer (:312-318); the label `Previewing: 16:20 — Changed style` (:326-330); a 0-100 range slider (:331-348); a three-part time row start / current / end (:349-355); "Restore this point" (:359-365) and "Exit time-travel  Ctrl+Shift+T" (:366-371). Empty state at :319-322 "No history entries to scrub through." — which is what EVERY fresh reload produces, per FIG-G-01. Keyboard at :269-286: Left/Right step, bare Enter restores (see W-H-02), Ctrl+Shift+T exits.

claim: Every version row carries a change badge — "Auto-save · 3 changes · 16:20", "1 change", "2 changes", "Ali · 8 changes" — on all five Saves boards that inherit this list.
truth: On a freshly opened editor NO row carries a badge, because the count is derived from the in-memory undo stack and that stack is empty after a load. The badge only starts appearing for versions taken later in the same session. The board draws the exception as the rule.
evidence: VersionHistoryPanel.tsx:273-277 `const { historyStack } = useHistoryState(composer); versionChangeCounts(versions, historyStack)`. versionChangeCounts.ts:46 `if (versions.length === 0 || history.length === 0) return counts;` — an empty stack returns an empty map, and :54 `if (n > 0) counts.set(...)` omits zeros deliberately. VersionList.tsx:174 `{changeCount !== undefined && (` — absent id, no badge. The stack is empty on load: HistoryManager.ts:156-160 resets it on PROJECT_LOADED and HistoryFormatter.ts:21 skips the seed checkpoint.
edit: Redraw 162:2's default rows WITHOUT the change badge (name · Auto · time only), and add the badge as a labelled variant with a note: "shown only for versions taken since this tab opened — the count comes from the session's undo stack." Same rows are inherited by 163:113, 163:167, 163:220 and 163:269.

truth: A Saves row shows no author at all, and the product has no display name for an editor user anywhere in History. Attribution IS recorded now (a user id), but the row never reads it, and the one place any author reaches the screen renders the FIRST CHARACTER of a cuid — so every chip reads the same letter.

The approval band's reviewer name is different and IS real (SavesChrome.tsx:117-123 reads `review.reviewerName` and drops the clause when absent) — leave that alone.

claim: The list's shape is three auto-saves inside 70 minutes (16:20, 16:05, 15:10) around one named version — i.e. a product that checkpoints on a cadence.
truth: There is no cadence. Auto-checkpoints fire on exactly ONE event, `template:applied`, plus the safety version taken before a restore. The interval field that would give a cadence is declared, defaulted, and read by nothing. A user who never applies a template and never restores has zero auto-saves, and the section's own empty board already states the true rule.
evidence: shared/types/versions.ts:88 `autoCheckpointEvents: ["template:applied"]` with the founder note at :83-87 recording that `project:loaded` was removed on 2026-09-02; VersionTimelineManager.ts:140-149 subscribes to exactly that list. `autoCheckpointInterval` has exactly two references in packages/editor/src — its declaration (versions.ts:70) and its default (:82) — and no consumer. The only other producer of an auto-row is the restore safety save (VersionTimelineManager.ts:291-294), which is a NAMED version. Board 163:64 already says it correctly: "Versions are created whenever you name one, or when a template is applied."
edit: Rebalance 162:2's sample list toward named versions with at most one "Auto-save", and add the rule as a note on the board: "Auto-saves happen when a template is applied — there is no timed checkpoint." (Sample data is not conformed literally, but a list whose shape is 3:1 auto-to-named asserts a cadence the product does not have.)

claim: 163:269 is the only storage-pressure state in the section: auto-saves aged out, all is well, amber.
truth: There is a second, worse storage state the code produces and no board draws: the version store is full and the save is REFUSED. The quota path prunes 10 and retries once, but the prune only ever deletes auto-checkpoints, so a user whose versions are all named gets a prune of 0 and a second throw — surfacing as a bare red "Save failed" toast with no reason and no way out. Nothing anywhere monitors quota before that point.
evidence: VersionHistoryStorage.ts:91-105 saveVersion: on QuotaExceededError it calls `pruneVersions(projectId, versions.length - 10)` (:99) then `await writeVersion(version)` (:100) with no second catch; pruneVersions returns 0 when `toDelete.length === 0` (:240-242) because :236-238 filters to `isAutoCheckpoint`. The rejection reaches VersionHistoryPanel.tsx:183 `pushToast("Save failed", "error")` — five characters, no cause. Nothing pre-empts it: StorageAdapter.ts:412-436 `getStorageQuota()` has zero callers in packages/editor/src outside its own tests, and `STORAGE_QUOTA_WARNING` / `STORAGE_QUOTA_CRITICAL` (events.ts:454-455, payloads at :882-883, thresholds at config.ts:149-150) are named nowhere else — searched by constant.
edit: New board "History · Saves · save-failed (store full)", cloned from 163:269's notice band in the error tint: title "This version could not be saved", body "Your version history is full on this device. Export your versions or delete some to make room.", two actions Export / Manage. Plus a warning variant of the same band for the 80% threshold the config already defines.

claim: Nothing in section 16 draws what a user sees when they reopen a site whose last save never reached the server — the state the whole unsaved-work module exists to produce.
truth: On reopen with a kept record the editor does three things at once and none of them is boarded here: the topbar save chip goes red with "This site has edits that never reached the server.", a warning toast with duration Infinity appears carrying a "Restore my edits" action, and the on-screen project is the SERVER's, not the user's. Restoring is a whole-project import with no comparison against what the server now holds.
evidence: useComposerInit.ts:229-253 — `const unsaved = readUnsaved(siteId)`; when non-null it sets `{status:'error', error:'This site has edits that never reached the server.'}` and raises the toast titled "Some work never reached the server" with the body "A save failed before this page was reloaded. The version on screen is the server's. Restoring puts your unsaved edits back so you can save them again.", `duration: Infinity`, action label "Restore my edits" whose onClick is `instance.importProject(unsaved.project); setIsDirty(true); … clearUnsaved(siteId)` (:245-250). The record: unsavedRecovery.ts:23 `bk-unsaved-v1-`, :27 keyed per site, :38-45 localStorage write inside an empty catch, :29-33 the shape is `{project, at}` — no server revision, so the restore cannot know the server moved on. It is written on exactly two branches, both network-only: useSaveCallback.ts:178 and useComposerInit.ts:590.

NOTE FOR THE COORDINATOR, not filed here because the nodes are outside this manifest: the existing recovery art — 307:2223 "C6 · Recovery banner" (section 862:6859) and 297:2027 "S1.2 · crash-recovery" (section 1776:8388) — both draw a BANNER, while the code ships a toast plus a chip; and the component that IS a banner (RecoveryBanner.tsx:52-82) fires off the crash sentinel alone (:55 `RecoveryManager.consumeLastCrash()`) and claims "Recovered your work · N pages" for work nothing kept. Those two boards need the same pass.

claim: The conflict dialog is attributed and offers a merge review: "Someone else saved first" / "Sara saved a change to this page 40 seconds ago. Keeping yours will overwrite hers." with Review both · Save backup · Keep mine.
truth: RECOMMENDATION: fix-board, with a node-level NOT-IMPLEMENTED note on the two parts that need code that does not exist. (a) The attribution is unbuildable today: the conflict signal carries a timestamp and nothing else, and the server has no column recording who saved. (b) The conflict is site-level, not "this page". (c) "Review both" has no destination: there is no local-vs-server diff anywhere in the product. (d) The three real actions are Reload latest / Save a backup / Overwrite… → a second-step "Yes, overwrite" with an amber warning — and the board's set contains no reload at all, though its own topbar chip says "Conflict — reload". (e) Correct as drawn: that chip. It matches the shipping copy and the state is produced.

(b) same check, keyed on the Site row. (c) the two comparators both take stored artefacts, never the server's newer project: VersionTimelineManager.ts:730 compareVersions(currentId, targetId) diffs two stored NamedVersions, and approvedCompare.ts:220 compareApprovedToCurrent diffs a review snapshot against a live export; the conflict path never fetches the server copy — AquibraStudio.tsx:687 `onReload={() => window.location.reload()}`. (d) ConflictModal.tsx:52-69 — title "This site changed somewhere else", body "Your copy is behind — it was edited in another tab or device since you opened it. We can't auto-merge, so pick how to continue. Nothing is lost without your choice.", buttons at :63-69 with the two-step overwrite and the amber line at :57-60. (e) SaveStatus.tsx:44 `conflict: "Conflict — reload"`, produced at useSaveCallback.ts:146 `setSaveState((prev) => ({ ...prev, status: "conflict" }))` and derived at StudioHeader.tsx:564-565.
edit: On 66:640: replace the dialog title and body with the shipping copy above; replace the action row with Reload latest (primary) · Save a backup · Overwrite… and add the second-step state ("Yes, overwrite" in red with the amber warning line). Keep the topbar chip as drawn. If the founder wants to KEEP the attributed design as a target instead, do not rename the whole shell board — attach a NOT IMPLEMENTED note to the two nodes only (the "Sara saved…" text and the "Review both" button), naming the cost: a `Site.lastEditedById` column plus a local-vs-server diff surface. Corroborating design-ahead art, outside this manifest: 807:6965 "S1.2d - Conflict - Review both (Compare opens with conflict context)" in section 862:6859.

Each pane is a sandboxed frame and they scroll independently — the labels carry the asymmetry, not colour." claim: The list draws item-level change rows, resolving individual elements: read off 168:48 with an explicit instance-descending walk, the five rows are "Hero · headline / edited", "Hero · subtitle / edited", "Opening hours / edited", "Gallery / 2 images added", "Happy hour banner / deleted" — two of them are separate elements INSIDE one hero section.
truth: The comparator works one level up, at PAGE STRIPS — the direct children of the exported page root. A headline and a subtitle inside the same hero produce ONE row, not two, labelled by the section's first heading. A button, an image or a caption changed deep inside a section is reported against the section. That is a deliberate choice recorded in the code, and no board or caption in the family says it, so anyone building to 168:48 will build rows the comparator cannot emit.
evidence: approvedCompare.ts:6-22 docblock: "This comparator works one level up: it matches the page's top-level STRIPS (the sections a client thinks in) by identity, so a strip inserted at the top reads as one 'added', not fifty 'changed'." Implementation: :133-150 extractStrips takes `Array.from(onlyChild.children)` where onlyChild is the page-root wrapper (:138-143); identity is `el.classList[0]` — the `<cssPrefix><elementId>` class ExportEngine emits — falling back to `<tag>#<index>` (:145); the label is the strip's first heading text clipped to 40 chars, or its semantic tag name (:75-85). The only per-strip signals are whole-strip text and a style signature: :209-214 `if (s.text !== c.text) … "Text changed"` and `if (s.styleSig !== c.styleSig) … "Style changed"`.
edit: Add a note to 168:48 (and to the family entry 168:2): "Rows are page SECTIONS, not elements — a change anywhere inside a section reports once, against the section." claim: Section 17 is called "Compare" and reads as THE compare surface of the editor.
truth: There are two compare engines in the product with two different vocabularies, and this family describes only one of them. The word "Compare" appears on both doors and means different things: the approval band's "Compare with current" opens THIS family (approved snapshot vs live site, five kinds: added / removed / moved / content / style, strip-level, iframes); the per-row "Compare" in the Saves list opens a different component entirely (version snapshot vs version snapshot, five DIFFERENT kinds: style / text / layout / content / other plus page add/remove counts, element-level, no render). A third — the published-version diff — exists too and is W-N-23's row. A designer reading section 17 will assume it covers all of them.
